note: NEW RAD CITY (https://newrad.city/play) is capture-class: a Netlify deploy whose pretty-URL route /play serves the deploy's play.html (byte-identical at /play.html; /play/ 301-redirects to /play). One 22,667,976 B document holds the whole game — the project's own single-file build inlining 629 source modules as 630 inline <script> blocks (22,515,466 B), each opening with its own `/* src/<dir>/<file>.js */` banner and wrapped in a single IIFE (`(function () { 'use strict'; … })();`), plus 12 inline <style> blocks (139,891 B) with their own `/* …css */` banners, over a small UI markup shell. §0.4 fork-over-mirror was checked on 2026-10-13 — see README (no public upstream repo for the project itself; the only repository credits in the captured text are library/author links, and GitHub searches for the game's name and author return nothing) — so the mirror stands. Derived pipeline: capture → pinned prettier 3.9.6 (module API, default options, format-to-fixed-point — most blocks are stable after one pass, a few member-chain reflows need up to 3; the per-source prettyPasses count is recorded; never the CLI: it respects .gitignore and can silently echo its input) → every inline content block becomes a readable twin (readable/play-inline-<N>.pretty.js for scripts #1..630 in document order, readable/play-inline-<N>.pretty.css for styles #1..12; every twin provably NOT byte-identical to its capture block; readable/index-inline-map.json records each block's exact byte range + sha256 + module banner), and the captured Netlify RUM beacon (.netlify/scripts/rum, an extensionless minified JS route) becomes readable/netlify-rum.pretty.js. Script twins are then cut into statement-aligned slices src/<tag>-NN.js: the module IIFE is unwrapped and only its body's top-level statement boundaries are used (~250-350 line windows; oversized single declarations stay whole), with the exact 2-line provenance header. Statements that cannot stand alone (the IIFE wrapper head/tail, and top-level `return` guard clauses inside the module IIFE) are indexed as skipped sections, never sliced. Every slice parses standalone under `node --input-type=module --check -` and round-trips byte-exact to its recorded readable line range. Stylesheet rule — the 12 inline <style> blocks are wholeFile sections, never sliced. Non-code payloads: none are captured (the game is fully procedural; no same-origin asset requests exist); the notRendered array is kept for the record. The off-origin loads (three.js 0.158.0 from cdn.jsdelivr.net, the Google Fonts stylesheets/font origins) were never captured (socker precedent, PLAN §1) and have no derived layer; tools/capture.mjs --check lists them as external references. Identifiers in src/ are the capture's own names (the modules are unminified project source) — the rename campaign (PLAN §5) is recorded as an open task in README.md, not claimed here. Capture bytes are untouched by everything above; re-cut with `node tools/derive.mjs` after any capture refresh. `node tools/audit.js` is the gate.

renderOptions._default: prettier 3.9.6, module API, default options, format-to-fixed-point (re-format until the output is stable — recorded per source as prettyPasses; most are 1, a few need 2-3) — never the CLI: it respects .gitignore and can silently echo its input
renderOptions.js: parser babel, no plugins (inline <script> blocks + the captured extensionless RUM beacon)
renderOptions.json: parser json, no plugins (inline importmap blocks, if any)

The off-origin <link rel=stylesheet> (Google Fonts) and the jsdelivr three.js <script src> are CDN dependencies and are not derived.
